topic: How does defocused reflector gain loss impact link budget margins for SNR compared to conventional designs?
consensus_response: Defocused reflectors introduce increased path loss due to wider beam patterns, leading to amplified interference and degraded SNR. This translates to higher channel utilization and reduced throughput, impacting link budget margins. Adaptive beamforming techniques can mitigate this issue by dynamically adjusting beam directionality, but their implementation requires sophisticated receiver design for dynamic directionality adjustments.
reference_context: Defocused reflectors amplify signal-level noise due to wider beam patterns, increasing interference between adjacent beams. This results in reduced gain and increased path loss, directly impacting link budget margins. The spatial arrangement of defocused beams at the array borders contributes significantly to this effect due to increased spillover loss.  Adaptive beamforming techniques can mitigate this issue but require sophisticated receiver design for dynamic directionality adjustments.
